acquisition method: top 10 most abundant ions were selected for isolation and fragmentation
alkylation reagent: followed by alkylation with 10 mM iodoacetamide for 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
alkylation concentration: followed by alkylation with 10 mM iodoacetamide for 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
cleavage agent: digested overnight at room temperature with Lys-C (1:200 enzyme to protein ratio) followed by dilution to 1.5M urea and 4 hour digestion with trypsin (1:200 enzyme to protein ratio).
collision energy: Normalized collision energies were set to 35%... Normalized collision energies were set to 25%.
fractionation method: HEK293 cell peptides were separated by basic pH reverse phase fractionation that was performed on ~0.5 mg sample.
fragmentation method: top 20 most abundant ions were selected for isolation and fragmentation by HCD.
instrument: LTQ Orbitrap Elite, Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometer

analyzed by LC-ESI-MS/MS on a hybrid dual-pressure linear ion trap/orbitrap mass spectrometer (LTQ Orbitrap Elite, Thermo Scientific, San Jose, CA)... Basic pH reverse phase fractions from HEK293 cells were analyzed on a Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometer.
ionization type: Liquid chromatography electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (LC-ESI-MS/MS)
labeling: In a proteome-wide dataset on HEK293 cells (9,513 proteins and 396,736 peptides)
reduction reagent: The lysate was reduced with 5 mM dithiothreitol for 30 minutes at 56ºC
reduction concentration: The lysate was reduced with 5 mM dithiothreitol for 30 minutes at 56ºC
